## About
Modderman Service is a Porsche specialty family business on Wyandotte Street in Mountain View. Second-generation owner and technician David Modderman puts it simply: "Detailed knowledge has been handed down from one generation to the next." The shop works on everything from the earliest models to the newer Porsche SUVs, using the most sophisticated Porsche scanner, current factory information including updates, and high-quality factory parts.
The shop moved from its old home on Old Middlefield Way to a much larger building just down the road. There's a window in the front office so you can see what's going on in the garage, a big driveway with no backing out, and garage storage so cars are kept inside at night.
Customers rate the shop 4.8 from 85 Google reviews. One reviewer wrote that Dave, Steve and the team "really know their stuff" and remember their customers' names.

## Services
- Brake Service: Technicians check brake fluid level, quality and moisture, pad wear, rotor thickness, wheel hubs and brake lines. Worn parts are replaced with OEM parts, and pads can be upgraded for hard and track driving.
- Air Conditioning Service: Evacuation of any moisture, recharging the system with the proper amount of freon, and a visual inspection of the whole A/C system. Leaks at the hoses, fittings and front condenser are repaired.
- Check Engine Light On: Diagnosis with the shop's Porsche scanner and software.
- Factory Recommended Services: Scheduled maintenance for your Porsche, with access to the latest factory information and updates for newer models.
- Cooling System Service: Cooling system work on Porsches. One reviewer had a water pump and belt tensioner replaced here.

## FAQ
Q: Which Porsches do you work on?
A: The 356, 911, 914, 912, 968, 944, Cayman, Boxster and Panamera, along with the newer Porsche SUVs.

Q: How do I make an appointment?
A: Call (650) 967-3213 or email dave@modderman.com. One reviewer suggests booking well ahead because the shop stays busy.

Q: How often should my brake fluid be flushed?
A: David suggests every two years. Brake fluid absorbs moisture over time, which lowers its boiling point and can let the pedal sink.

Q: How often should the A/C be serviced?
A: Every two years. David says most of what can go wrong in an A/C system can be prevented with a regular two-year service.

Q: Where is my car kept overnight?
A: Inside. The shop garage-stores cars at night to protect them from the elements and vandalism.
